title: Simple flower outline
subtitle: Six petals and a French knot centre worked from a traced template
excerpt: A six-petal flower outline is the classic second project in surface embroidery: stem stitch petals, lazy daisy or detached chain alternatives, and a cluster of French knots at the centre.
heroPrompt: Simple six-petal embroidered flower on cream linen, stem stitch outline petals in coral pink, French knot centre in yellow, inside a 15 cm hoop, natural light.

content.text: A simple flower outline uses two stitches: stem stitch for the petal outlines, and French knots for the centre. The same template works for lazy daisy petals instead; both versions practice transferring a design and following curves.

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Natural or white cotton, 20 x 20 cm

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton in 2 colours (one for petals, one for centre), 2 strands

content.text: Draw a flower template: a central circle of about 1 cm, with 6 oval petals radiating from it at equal spacing. Trace onto the fabric.
Mount the fabric in the hoop. Work stem stitch around each petal outline, starting at the base and working around to the tip and back.
Fill the central circle with 5 to 7 French knots clustered together.
Remove the transfer marks with a damp cloth. Leave to dry.
To vary the project: replace stem stitch petals with lazy daisy petals for a softer look, or add a stem line in stem stitch below the flower.
